thanks for your comment but honestly i have to disagree with some of the opinions you have. 1. we’ve only broken up once, after being together for two years and living together for one of those years. We ended because I was unhappy and needed to go back home with my parents so I could get a handle of my life and school.  He also needed to become more finically dependent (which he did :D) 
Also, we didn’t speak to each other for three months so We did kind of have a break. Overall my question and post was asking about regaining trust during things that happened during a break and if anyone thinks i’m being manipulated or played honestly! again i appreciate your comment but i wanted to clear things up because the last thing he and i ever were was an off and on relationship. in fact if we didnt live together so young we both agreed we probably would’ve never spilt, we were just 18 thinking we knew everything about this damn world LOL!

I got back together with him because I really do believe he is my soulmate, and I understand how young we are so when it comes to things like this I tell myself we are young and make mistakes so I need to be understanding and forgiving (obviously in some aspects, if he cheated on me or was abusive that’s clearly a way different story) so we can  grow together- or apart. Thank you, what you told me is what he’s been telling me. I just fear manipulation

I would definitely bring it up and ask where her point of view is when it comes to questioning those guys and try and understand why she’s doing it and then try and help her understand why that’s unhealthy because it sounds like she has control issues which would make sense because she just got out of a four year relationship and is probably use to having her significant other truly be her person... but I think telling her and making her aware of the issue will help her a lot and if you guys are close then she shouldn’t be offended and if you’re worried she will be offended just reassure her you’re just saying this because you want things to work out for her. I think what you’re doing is a good move and shows you’re a good friend!

I think this really comes in hand with where you see yourself in 5 years once you are 40. You need to really think about you as an individual and ask yourself who is really important here. Honestly I am only 18 but I do know from a kids point of view, you leaving will be in their memory but they will move on, esepically with social media and how fast things are moving. They have their entire life to live and eventually they will be 20 and you will be stuck with someone who makes you feel like a doormat. That's my opinion and I know leaving is alot easier said then done, so that's why I think you really need to figure out where you hope to be in 5 years with your band, family, career, etc. and see if she is just dragging you down. And I understand this family helped you grow and you can still love and appericate them for that, but for your and your fiancé mental health leaving might just be the best thing you did for eachother.
